result.summary: The scoped diff adds a held decision point for failed execute children. It has a failed-keyed payload, a superseded/fix-round exclusion, resolution when the task leaves failed, and a worktree note in the packet. The two new tests, test_failed_execute_with_dependents_yields_point and test_superseded_failed_task_yields_no_point, exercise the creation, resolution and supersession paths. Changes stay within the two scoped files. I found no trust-boundary or privilege issue: the worktree note uses git read-only commands and the data is fenced as before.

comments.issue: A failed execute child only yields a point when it has a status=failed event, because _failed_key returns None otherwise. A task set to failed without an event is silently skipped, so its dependents stay blocked. The events are written by the normal bus.update path, so this is an edge case.

Fix round 1 changed no code. The red gate came from test_spawn.RunClaudeNormalisedUsage, a suite-order flake outside this task's scope. That test is not in the diff and the acceptance criteria name only the two planner_runs tests and tests.test_planner_runs, so it does not block approval. I did not re-run the tests myself.
